themes_detail.label: Tree damage surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints exploded to 18 THIS WEEK—a 414% spike versus 3.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 14.5)—suggesting either severe weather, construction damage, or a localized tree-health crisis requiring urgent Parks Department investigation.
evidence: 18 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.5 weekly average (414% increase, z-score: 14.5)
5 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.6 average (700% spike, z-score: 9.04)
Concurrent street condition spike (56 complaints this week vs. 18.4 avg) suggests possible weather or construction event
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about what triggered the tree damage wave this week—weather, disease, or construction?
Map where complaints are concentrated; talk to residents about trees down in their blocks

themes_detail.label: Street deterioration accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked 205% THIS WEEK to 56 complaints versus 18.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.55), indicating either weather damage, pothole outbreak, or deferred maintenance becoming visible—aligns with repeated CB budget requests for street reconstruction.
evidence: 56 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 18.4 weekly average (205% increase, z-score: 5.55)
Correlates with tree damage spike, suggesting possible weather event or systemic maintenance gap
Community Board has filed repeated capital budget requests for street reconstruction—chronic unmet need
reporting_angles: Obtain DOT pothole data for CD310 this week; cross-reference 311 complaints with actual repair permits filed
Interview DOT about whether street maintenance backlog is contributing; talk to residents about worst-affected blocks

themes_detail.label: Illegal tree cutting spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints jumped 700% last week to 5 versus 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.04), suggesting either coordinated tree removal activity, contractor violations, or encroachment—requires DOB and Parks investigation.
evidence: 5 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 9.04)
391 building alteration permits filed in 90-day period; 322 are alterations (potential correlation with tree damage)
Concurrent damaged tree spike suggests coordinated or cascading event
reporting_angles: File FOIL for DOB enforcement actions on tree removal violations in CD310 over past 2 weeks
Interview Parks Enforcement and residents about whether illegal clearing is tied to development activity

themes_detail.label: Sanitation deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Dirty condition complaints surged 150% last week to 39 versus 15.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.51), and noise complaints jumped 332% to 27 versus 6.2 average—suggesting possible sanitation service gap or event spillover, aligns with CB's repeated garbage collection infrastructure requests.
evidence: 39 dirty condition complaints last week vs. 15.6 weekly average (150% increase, z-score: 5.51)
27 noise/street-sidewalk complaints last week vs. 6.2 weekly average (332% increase, z-score: 4.59)
Community Board has filed repeated requests for garbage collection and recycling infrastructure—long-standing unmet need
reporting_angles: Check with DSNY on whether trash collection routes were disrupted last week in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights
Interview residents on worst blocks; photograph visible debris and sanitation conditions for visual story

themes_detail.label: Derelict vehicles and disorder uptick
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints jumped 216% last week to 17 versus 5.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.96), coupled with animal-in-park spike (500%, 3 complaints this week), signaling possible enforcement lapse or quality-of-life deterioration in public spaces.
evidence: 17 derelict vehicle complaints last week vs. 5.4 weekly average (216% increase, z-score: 4.96)
3 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 5.0)
Multi-faceted disorder signal (vehicles, animals, sanitation) suggests possible public-space enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Obtain NYPD and DSNY enforcement data for CD310 last week; identify which parks or blocks are concentration points
Interview Parks Department about animal control and abandoned-vehicle removal protocols
